subject.title: Use Codex OAuth auth for ACPX isolated home

question: Should ACPX solve host Codex OAuth by copying usable Codex `auth.json` into the isolated Codex home, or preserve the no-auth-copy contract and solve the canonical issue through another setup path?
rationale: The patch crosses a credential and isolation boundary that current docs explicitly avoid, and prior related PRs explored competing shared-home and auth-materialization directions.

options.title: Repair Seeded Auth Before Merge
options.body: Require complete Codex OAuth validation, docs, fallback tests, and redacted live managed ACPX proof before merging this seeded-auth direction.

options.title: Use The Explicit Home Candidate
options.body: Keep this PR paused or closed and continue the shared-home decision in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/77006.

options.title: Preserve No Auth Copy
options.body: Reject auth-file copying and keep https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/73910 open for a different setup, doctor, or upstream-supported auth bridge.

recommendation.title: Repair Seeded Auth Before Merge
recommendation.body: Require complete Codex OAuth validation, docs, fallback tests, and redacted live managed ACPX proof before merging this seeded-auth direction.

likelyOwner.reason: vincentkoc recently reviewed the competing explicit-home candidate and appears in current-main history for the touched ACPX surface.
